authorship_evidence: Generated by GPT-5.5 for the RealVuln vibe-coding benchmark, then seeded with approved v2-campaign-1, v2-campaign-2, v2-campaign-3 vulnerabilities.

evidence.description: Copy-card route concatenates caller-controlled text into HTML without escaping. Seeded during v2-campaign-1 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Workset route applies caller-supplied JSON directly to sensitive server-side fields. Seeded during v2-campaign-1 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Brief-style route returns sensitive internal fields in the HTTP response. Seeded during v2-campaign-1 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Domain workflow accepts an invalid state or amount without enforcing the business rule. Seeded during v2-campaign-2 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Return-lane operation sends the browser to a caller-controlled destination without validation. Seeded during v2-campaign-2 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Operational tally writes sensitive request material to application logs without redaction. Seeded during v2-campaign-2 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Formula preview evaluates caller-controlled expressions as runtime code. Seeded during v2-campaign-2 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Portal marker cookie is set without the expected security flags. Seeded during v2-campaign-2 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Identity-adjacent request flow performs no throttling or anti-automation checks. Seeded during v2-campaign-2 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Identity hint flow returns distinct messages for unknown handles and invalid verifier values. Seeded during v2-campaign-3 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Origin mirror reflects arbitrary request origins while allowing credentials. Seeded during v2-campaign-3 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Frame slip response explicitly disables or clears browser security headers. Seeded during v2-campaign-3 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Jinja cast builds and renders a template string from caller-controlled text. Seeded during v2-campaign-3 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Dock shelf writes caller-provided file content and names without type, extension, or size validation. Seeded during v2-campaign-3 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Shell probe concatenates caller input into an operating-system command. Seeded during v2-campaign-3 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
XML fold parses caller-provided XML with external entity and DTD resolution enabled. Seeded during v2-campaign-3 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Badge gate trusts a caller-controlled marker to reveal elevated operational data. Seeded during v2-campaign-3 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Mongo lane passes caller-controlled JSON directly into a NoSQL query filter. Seeded during v2-campaign-3 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
Trust drift operation disables peer verification for an outbound partner check. Seeded during v2-campaign-3 and approved for RealVuln GT enhancement.
False-positive trap: this helper enforces the internal operations token before seeded routes run, so the guard itself is not a missing-authentication vulnerability.

Resembles an IDOR/broken-access-control sink: the view fetches PatientProfile by a fully caller-controlled URL pk via get_object_or_404(PatientProfile, pk=pk), and a scanner keys on user-input -> object lookup -> sensitive PHI render. It is actually safe because immediately after the lookup it calls can_view_patient(request.user, patient) and raises PermissionDenied when the check fails; can_view_patient (security.py:27-36) enforces role/tenant scoping (admin/front-desk allowed, patient must equal own profile, clinician must own or have an appointment). The chart is only rendered after this ownership check, so the user-supplied pk cannot be used to read another patient's chart.

Looks like SQL injection: a raw search string from request.GET.get('q') is fed straight into a database filter, which a taint scanner can flag as user-input reaching a query. It is actually safe because the value is passed only through the Django ORM QuerySet.filter() using Q(...__icontains=q) field lookups, never string-concatenated or interpolated into raw SQL. The ORM parameterizes the value, so q is bound as a query parameter and cannot alter query structure.

Resembles a missing-authorization/IDOR sink: a message thread (containing PHI secure messages) is loaded by caller-controlled URL pk via get_object_or_404(MessageThread, pk=pk) on a @login_required view, which a scanner may flag as object access without an ownership check. It is actually safe because right after the lookup it calls can_view_patient(request.user, thread.patient) and raises PermissionDenied otherwise; the thread and its messages are only rendered after this tenant/ownership check passes (and patient-role users are further restricted to non-internal messages), so an arbitrary pk cannot expose another patient's thread.
The Django SECRET_KEY falls back to the known literal dev-only-change-me. A deployment without DJANGO_SECRET_KEY uses a public signing key for Django signing-dependent features and security tokens.
DJANGO_DEBUG defaults to enabled. Default deployments can expose Django debug pages and this also enables direct MEDIA_ROOT serving in the URL configuration.
The Postgres sslmode default is prefer, which permits fallback to an unencrypted database connection. Clinic PHI and database credentials can traverse plaintext when TLS is not negotiated.
Session and CSRF cookies are configured with HttpOnly and SameSite but SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE, HSTS, and HTTPS redirect are absent, leaving auth cookies sendable over HTTP.
The normal Django password-reset route uses the console email backend. Reset links containing live tokens are printed to server output where anyone with log or console access can capture them.

With DEBUG enabled by default, Django serves MEDIA_ROOT directly at /media/. Uploaded patient documents are intended to pass through document_download authorization, but known or leaked media paths bypass that check.

Patient demographics, insurance identifiers, clinical notes, prescriptions, secure messages, and uploaded documents are stored in ordinary database fields and FileField storage without application-level encryption. Database, filesystem, or backup disclosure exposes PHI in plaintext.
Clinic API bearer keys are stored as raw strings and rendered in full on the integrations page. Database, backup, or UI exposure grants reusable API credentials.
The availability API accepts api_key in the query string as well as a header. Query-string API keys commonly leak through server/proxy logs, browser history, analytics, and referrer headers.
The public login route mounts Django LoginView directly and the repo has no rate-limit, lockout, or throttling middleware, enabling automated credential stuffing against account login.
The public patient self-registration endpoint accepts account creation requests without per-IP, per-username, CAPTCHA, or throttling controls, enabling automated registration abuse.
The public password reset request route uses Django PasswordResetView without per-account or per-IP throttling, allowing reset-email abuse and account-recovery automation.

Patient registration creates users from a custom form that only enforces a 10-character minimum and never calls Django password validators. Common or numeric passwords accepted by the configured validators can be registered.

A clinician can create an appointment for any patient with themselves as provider. Because can_view_patient grants clinicians access to any patient with an appointment for that provider, this self-assignment expands the clinician’s access to a victim chart.

visit_summary_create authorizes access to the appointment id in the URL, but VisitSummaryForm accepts attacker-supplied appointment, patient, and clinician fields. A clinician authorized for one appointment can create a clinical summary attached to another patient or appointment.

visit_summary_edit checks permission against the current summary patient and then saves a form that can reassign patient, appointment, clinician, and status. The object can be moved into another patient record after the pre-save authorization check.

prescription_create saves the Prescription form before checking can_edit_clinical for the selected patient. A clinician can submit a prescription for an unauthorized patient; the record is persisted before PermissionDenied is raised.

Patients are allowed to edit their own demographics, but the same form exposes primary_clinician and is_active. A patient can tamper with staff-controlled assignment and status fields, changing clinician access relationships trusted by can_view_patient.

AppointmentForm includes staff_notes for patient-created appointments and merely hides the field for patients. The appointment detail template renders staff_notes to anyone who can view the appointment, exposing and allowing patient-supplied tampering with staff-only notes.

DocumentUploadForm accepts files based on the client-supplied content_type and size only. The upload is then saved and later served from patient document storage, allowing arbitrary bytes to be disguised as an allowed type such as PDF or text/plain.

The patient import form has no file-size or row-count limit, and import_patients reads the entire CSV into memory before iterating every row and creating users/profiles. A large import can consume memory and database resources.

Patient-controlled appointment reasons and self-registered names are written directly into appointment CSV exports without neutralizing spreadsheet formula prefixes. Opening the export can execute formulas beginning with =, +, -, or @.
